Reasoning:

The request has two goals: (1) mechanistically quantify how precipitation splits into runoff, ET, and recharge across the Naches HUC8, and (2) validate against available observations. Naches has strong relief (352–1977 m, ~1625 m). Critically, this basin is inside CONUS, so the default NLDAS-2 forcing (~12 km) DOES resolve orographic precipitation and temperature across elevation — a basin of this relief spans ~15 distinct precip cells. This means the elevation → precip/snow → partitioning pathway IS partially representable here (unlike a uniform-forcing case), so elevation is a legitimate stratification axis, with the caveat that sub-12 km terrain (ridgetops) is smoothed and ridgetop SWE will be underestimated. Soil texture (SSURGO) and forcing period are the other levers.

Feasibility: ET, surface runoff, and recharge partitioning across soil × elevation ARE answerable, but recharge and any water-table target REQUIRE spin-up — I specify the WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) per column, which scales to CONUS. Snow/SWE is in default output → SNOTEL comparison is possible (6 co-located stations). WTD wells → co-located comparison at wells clamped to ELM's aquifer range. The stream-gauge validation is the honest gap: single-column ELM has no lateral routing, so 93 gauges cannot be matched natively — it needs a routing/aggregation step, which I flag under requires_capabilities and do NOT claim to deliver.

N: 4 elevation bands × 3 dominant soil classes ≈ 12 exploratory columns to span the driver matrix, concentrated at valley bottoms/riparian (recharge–soil-moisture exchange) and the rain-snow transition (~1000–1500 m, where partitioning is most sensitive). Validation columns are pinned to data: 6 SNOTEL + a modest set of accessible WTD wells.
